rulings: CF-ONE-SALE-ONE-ADDRESS (2026-09-05): one eBay sale resident under two cardId partitions is a split pool AND a double count. Never a delete - RETIRE marks flaggedWrong, PARK marks identityUnverified, and both are reversible.

NONE of these 7 is covered by 2026-09-05-twin-address-dedup.json, 2026-09-06-readback-verify-twins.json or 2026-09-06-readback-found-nothing-twins.json - verified by grepping every sale id against backend/data/. All 7 are new.

ONE CAUSE, MEASURED. All 7 copies that carry a stamp were rekeyed by the SAME fleet inside 42 seconds (2026-09-06T03:43:07Z-03:43:48Z) with reason 'GREAT REMATCH (2026-09-01): IMPROVE, checklist-backed, ...'. In each case the relocate wrote the keeper and did not delete the old row - the CF-A-VERIFY-MISMATCH-IS-A-DUPLICATE-NOT-A-FAILURE surface, so the sale is resident twice and NO sale was lost.

THE KEEPER IS DECIDED BY PROVENANCE, NOT BY ADDRESS. In all 7 groups exactly one copy is both STAMPED (rekeyedAt + rekeyedFrom naming the very address being retired) and CHECKLIST-BACKED (its cardId resolves in card_catalog). The rival copy is unstamped AND its address 404s against the catalog.

'bowman' for a Pokemon card, 'unknown', and 'player-' keys are NEVER keepers. Three of the retired addresses are exactly those - hiq:pokemon:2005:bowman:9, hiq:pokemon:2005:bowman:player-pokemon-ex-emerald-sceptile, hiq:pokemon:2016:unknown:8114 - and in every one of them the keeper is a tcgdex-scraped checklist identity (ex9, xy11, sm1, sm2).

THE BASEBALL GROUP IS NOT A DONRUSS-VS-FINEST DISPUTE. The sale's own title states '2005 Topps Finest - Corey Dillon #72 X-Fractor /250' - it names Topps Finest outright and no Donruss product at all. It is a SPORT misfile: Corey Dillon is football, the rematch keeper is Lyle Overbay's baseball card, and no checklist-backed football Topps Finest #72 row exists. CF-NEVER-DEFAULT-TO-EITHER-SIDE: both copies PARK rather than one being guessed.
